proposals.relationship: With Keith Nield, Eley challenges Scott’s portrayal of their approach as a binary choice between discourse and materialist social history, while welcoming her insistence on sexed subjectivities (2000).
proposals.evidence_note: Primary printed pp. 83–84 freshly read, with preceding context on p. 82. The reply jointly credits Eley and Nield; this personal route projects their shared intervention, not an independent Eley-only argument. Their praise for Scott’s lucidity, acknowledgment of sexuality’s importance and agreement about Rancière qualify the criticism. Existing mixed debate edge_1169 remains unchanged.
